title: Korea's Kospi Plunges Below 5,000 as AI Fears Trigger
summary: South Korean chip stocks Samsung and SK Hynix tumbled over 10% each as AI regulation fears drove the Kospi below 5,000, erasing gains from the 2025 AI boom.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plunged over 10% each on November 5, 2026, dragging Korea's Kospi index down 8.8%.
- The selloff pushed the Kospi below the symbolic 5,000 level after falling 46% from its June 2026 record high.
- Investor panic followed US midterm elections amid fears that tighter AI regulations would constrain chipmaker growth and data center demand.


South Korean semiconductor giants Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix suffered devastating losses on November 5, 2026, as investor panic over potential AI regulation sent shockwaves through global chip markets. Both companies plummeted over 10% in early trading, dragging Korea's benchmark Kospi index down 8.8% and forcing the Korea Exchange to halt trading for 20 minutes shortly after the opening bell.


## Market Collapse Erases AI Boom Gains


The dramatic selloff pushed the Kospi below the psychologically significant 5,000 level, a milestone that President Lee Jae Myung had set as a 2025 target. The index had quickly surpassed that goal during the artificial intelligence boom that fueled chipmaker profits throughout early 2026, but has now fallen 46% from its June record high as doubts about AI growth prospects intensified.


Kim Dojoon, chief executive officer at Zian Investment Management, characterized the market action as reaching "the panic sell stage," noting that "most market participants would be forced to sell in today's market." The trading halt represented one of the most severe intraday disruptions in Korean market history.


## Release Date and Global Contagion


Officially launched on November 5, 2026, this wave of selling followed a global technology rout on November 4 that wiped out a record $2.3 trillion in market value from the Nasdaq 100, which dropped 6.4%. A closely-watched gauge of US semiconductor stocks plunged 12% on November 4, marking its worst single-day performance since the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020.


The timing of the collapse coincided with the aftermath of US midterm elections, where a Democrat sweep of Congress raised investor concerns about tighter regulatory oversight of artificial intelligence development and deployment.


## AI Regulation Fears Drive Exodus


Investors rushed to exit AI-related positions following expectations that new Congressional leadership would implement stricter AI regulations, potentially constraining growth for chipmakers and data center suppliers. Samsung and SK Hynix, both heavily exposed to AI chip demand through their memory and advanced semiconductor businesses, bore the brunt of the selling pressure.


The regulatory uncertainty threatens to disrupt the supply chains and revenue models that have driven extraordinary growth in Korean semiconductor exports over the past 18 months. Memory chip demand from hyperscale data centers building AI infrastructure had been a primary revenue driver for both companies.


## Semiconductor Sector Under Pressure


The Korean chip sector's vulnerability became apparent as the selloff intensified throughout the trading session. Beyond Samsung and SK Hynix, smaller semiconductor suppliers and equipment manufacturers also faced steep declines as investors reassessed the pace of AI infrastructure buildout.


Market analysts noted that the speed and severity of the decline caught many institutional investors off guard, forcing portfolio managers to liquidate positions to meet margin calls and risk management requirements. The trading halt provided a brief respite but failed to stem the broader selling momentum.


## What This Means


The Kospi's breach of the 5,000 level marks a critical turning point for Korean markets and raises questions about the sustainability of AI-driven tech valuations globally. With semiconductor stocks accounting for a substantial portion of Korean market capitalization, continued regulatory uncertainty could pressure the index further. Investors now face a challenging environment where AI growth assumptions that drove 2025 and early 2026 gains are being fundamentally reassessed in light of potential government intervention and oversight.
